And immediately after that, they had to be handed over to the competent investigative judge for further processing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What were the resources and capacities of the military judiciary during the war according to what you learned from the documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, is this during the whole war? That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps the General could tell us whether things improved or got worse. Based on the documents that he perused, could he tell us about the resources and capabilities of the military judiciary throughout the war, including the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The resources were limited. There was a lack of both judges and prosecutors, and even more restricted were financial resources as well as the space where those institutions operated. Things improved slightly as time went on. In any case, the resources were quite scarce.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Based on the documents that you perused, would you say that people were released from custody and then all the proceedings were stayed against them; or once they were released, did it happen sometimes that they were still put on trial and again remanded on custody?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When they were released, that meant that the investigation against them was completed but they -- the proceedings were not completed. The final release happened only when the proceedings were completed in one way or another, either by a conviction or by the proceedings being stayed for any other reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But when people were released to await trial, did that mean that they would never be put on trial?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The prosecutor implied that you didn't notice that you didn't highlight the fact that people were not remanded in custody -- one part of that remark was that people were tried only after the war was over and that before that, before they were put on trial, they were not remanded in custody. Do you know what the policy of this Tribunal is? How long did Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Seselj spend in prison before their trial started? I've been here for five years, mind you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And now can we look at the following issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, how did Mr. Brown represent the room [Realtime transcript read in error "rumour"] of which you said that it was deep in our territory? Did he represent it as a battle-field that was created by the Muslim forces or did he represent it as a calm area where we committed crimes against innocent civilians?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think that there's a problem with the transcript and also I'd like to know how this arises exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm interested in the entire implication of Mr. Brown findings that General Keserovic challenged. He said that the Serbs carried out attacks, that they took over power, and that they used minor incidents in order to retaliate against minority Muslims and Croats. I would like to know whether the general made the same discovery, did he find the same thing or did he find something else in those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, he appears, Mr. Karadzic, to be under the impression that he's on direct again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the transcript you raised is "rumour" Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's what I wondered. I -- normally I wouldn't interject for an obvious mistake, but I don't understand the question because of the error in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter believes that the word "rumour" should be replaced by the word "room" or area or territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Karadzic, can you assist us how this arose from the line of cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, I believe that General Keserovic's position was challenged and that was that deep in our territory we faced an armed rebellion that took people away from the front line, threatened their families, and that was a theatre of war which was created by terrorist groups in the depths of our territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Throughout the war those groups were being challenged and arrested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did Mr. Nicholls deal with this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. But it seems that I remember the answer better than the question. However, he did deal with that and he said that Mr. Brown had used minor incidents to launch fierce responses. That was the position of the Prosecutor. As a matter of fact, the prosecutor repeats Brown's position and Brown did say that in his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But General Keserovic dealt with it in his report. Are we going to conclude his evidence today or not?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Excellencies. I'm doing my best and I believe that we will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then shall we move on to your next topic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, can we look at 1D3771. Did you personally see documents -- created documents by which minorities were protected and crimes against them prosecuted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By the way, are you tendering the previous document, request for investigation?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that it is already in evidence under a P number.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. I don't have it with me at the moment, I can't give you the number, but I believe it's in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what this document is. It was issued on the 1st of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: First of all, tell us what this document is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of my daily reports that I issued as the commander of the battalion of the military police of the East Bosnia Corps. It was sent to the corps commander and it describes the work of the military police unit, i.e., of its duty service.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the following page in both languages. It might even be number 3 in English, page number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at the paragraph which starts with the words "an on-site inspection was carried out in Rodoljuba Colakovica Street." What was this about? What did you do as the military police?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second -- yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Objection: One, he's now going into the witness as a fact witness; two, this is well outside the ARK. When Mr. Brown testified on direct I tried to go into, for example, Directive 4 and some events in Eastern Bosnia because I thought it tied in to the report and we were pretty much limited to the -- for this type of evidence, crimes on the ground, et cetera, to the area of responsibility of the 1 KK and the municipalities in Eastern Bosnia of the ARK. So I don't think it's proper now to go into on re-direct to rebut the cross crimes in Bijeljina if that's what this is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this is relevant from the point of view of credibility because the conduct of the Serbian side was challenged during the cross-examination of this expert, and here he personally reaffirms his own credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we agree with Mr. Nicholls. Move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, you've told us that Major Marinic [as interpreted] told you in a conversation you had with him that General Mladic had given him a good reason why the registration of prisoners of war should stop.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeated it several times. He said that the registration should stop because they would be moved to wherever they wanted to go. After the families that had already been transported in the direction of Tuzla, they would follow. That was the reason that was given to me according to my best recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the participants this is from the Mladic trial on 12865.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When it comes to the registration of prisoners of war, was that a standard procedure in the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Transcript matters. At 101, line 10, should be Malinic, not Marinic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Malinic, yes, I'm sorry. Perhaps my articulation was not very good at this hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the registration of prisoners of war, is that standard procedure in the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The registration and also according them the status of prisoners of war and the rights enjoyed by POWs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the fate and procedure involving personal belongings of prisoners of war? Can they keep them or, according to regulations, were they taken away from them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Does not arise from any way from my cross.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, I think it does because the General was asked about that, why this was stopped, and it was suggested that it was stopped for criminal reasons. And also in particular the question of documents was referred to as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah, let's see the cite for that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure that was dealt with, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we upload -- if you could identify the page number, shall we take a look.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mladic, it was mentioned at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karadzic. Mr. Nicholls was referring to his cross-examination, whether your question now arises from his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that that is the case, but he seems to have caught me on my left foot so I cannot deal with all the transcript pages. So I'll move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, you were asked when you first heard of prisoners from Srebrenica being killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was asked, and I said when Drazen Erdemovic and Kremenovic were brought in, that was the first time that I found out about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I stand to be corrected, but asked in which case?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe in this case. I believe that even some doubt was expressed, that Mr. Nicholls dealt with that subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Having heard his cross-examination a while ago, I can't remember. Shall we continue, Mr. Nicholls? It has already been answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, but I believe I did not ask him when he first heard about executions in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, did you ever see any written report of the Army of Republika Srpska in which executions are mentioned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm absolutely confident that was not discussed. Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, he's now going through ... [Trial Chamber confers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My objection is it does not arise from the cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, it does arise from the cross because the cross attacked the credibility of General Keserovic on the fact that he knew that prisoners had been killed, particularly referencing Cerska in the 17th of July. So in order to show that that's not correct, to restore credibility, we're entitled to show that he didn't know during this period of time that any prisoners had been executed. And one way --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And how is it related to the report to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Because that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Because that's one way in which he may have learned whether or not prisoners had been executed and the fact that he -- whether or not he saw any written reports which indicated prisoners from Srebrenica had been executed is relevant to that issue of his knowledge which was raised as a credibility attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Since Mr. Robinson's dealing with it, he should be prepared. I'd like to know the page and line that I opened the door to that with.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: There's a whole raft of pages. I don't -- I can look them up very quickly, but all -- the whole cross-examination about Cerska and his responsibility for the terrain -- search of the terrain after the 16th and 17th of July raised the issue of his involvement with the events in Srebrenica and, in fact, Mr. Nicholls concluded with the question -- proposition that he was somehow concealing his knowledge of the crimes in Srebrenica, and therefore went to his credibility because he was trying to deny that he was the commander of those forces during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And it's very creative, but none of that raises or opens the door to questions about reports which he may have reviewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, your reliance on credibility seems to be a bit remote. The Chamber doesn't think this arose from the cross-examination. Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. It is with pleasure that I will accept Mr. Nicholls' position, namely, that the credibility of General Keserovic is not being brought into question. And now I'm going to go back to Kotor Varos and Vecici --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- where it was challenged that -- that political work was being done in terms of alleviating the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just for the record, I don't accept Mr. Keserovic's credibility.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then I should be allowed to strengthen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The way to strengthen it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's leave it. It's not -- I'll leave it at that. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 714, please, could we have a look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, it has been disputed that everything possible was done to alleviate the situation and to ensure conditions for civilians. There is a translation, there must be a translation, yes, please. Could you cast a glance at this. Do you know this document? It has to do with Vecici that we mentioned a moment ago and my position that they should be released and also this disagreement with the command. Do you know this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is from a session of the War Presidency of the municipality of Kotor Varos where your position was presented, namely, that the civilian population of Vecici should be released.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just a moment, Your Honour. No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3914, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is the 1st October -- no, 1st November.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see 1D3 from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, how much longer are you going to go for today? How much more would you need to conclude?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Until 3.00, Excellencies. If you would bear with me, I would finish by 3.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D9330, please. All of it seems to be in the English language. The original is not there, but I'll take a look at this. I'll read it. From the 14th of October, 1992, on the basis of the decision of the Presidency of Republika Srpska of the 14th of October, 1992, on the same day they passed a decision. [In English] "Enabling all armed persons on the territory of the Kotor Varos municipality to lay down their arms by 15th of October, 1992, by 1400 hours. "Persons are permitted to remain in their houses, with a full guarantee of their personal and property safety. Those who feel that the security provided in this area is not guaranteed will be enabled to leave the territory of Kotor Varos municipality and Republika Srpska unhindered, under the supervision of the International Red Cross." [Interpretation] Were you aware of this document and were you aware of this position of the authorities in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of this position. I was aware of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 819. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3915.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 819 now, please. Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened in the beginning of June, that is what this report refers to. So you see here Slavonski Brod, Derventa, and then the second paragraph: "In the area of Prijedor, Sanski Most, Kljuc ...," please go on.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are still --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not know where the witness is reading from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You're too fast. Where can we find the passage, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's actually the end of the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. "In the area of Prijedor, Sanski Most, and Kljuc there are still individuals and groups of extremists that are still active. "It is to be expected that there will be fighting in the entire area of responsibility and that new hotbeds of crisis will be opened up. The Ustasha attacks will focus on the areas of Jajce and Donji Vakuf."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page, please. Point 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, can you tell us what the losses of the 30th Partizan Division were from --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not catch the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- 14 soldiers, that is actually in paragraph 7 in our depth, that is what it looked like. How could we have 14 soldiers who were killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that is in three days only.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Brown, did he understand that these groups turned our rear into a front line, into a battle-field? Was that the right kind of appraisal?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Leading. And this -- just for the record, this is footnoted by Brown at 604 and 619. But I do object to that kind of leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now it's time to wrap up your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. But then I'd like to tender this document because it is in the footnote. And I withdraw that question about the 14 casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3916, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank the Chamber for this additional effort and the Prosecution as well and the interpreters and the Registry, and I would like to thank the General for his efforts made in order to work out this expert report and in terms of his testimony too. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, that concludes your evidence, General Keserovic. Thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There's one matter I'd like to deal with in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Tomorrow we'll resume at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon and start with Mr. Kljajic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 30th day of July, 2013, at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
